_comment: THE FIELD SET, CHOSEN FROM MEASURED EVIDENCE — 2026-08-03.
`ceiling` on each field is how many of the 57 documents state that field's gold value in
their prose AT ALL, measured by tools/build_corpus.py --ceiling. It is a property of the
corpus, not of any model: a field nothing states cannot be extracted by anything, so its
accuracy would be a fact about ClinicalTrials.gov's house style and not about the model.
FIVE FIELDS WERE CUT ON THIS EVIDENCE, and they were in the approved wireframe as
illustration: start_date (stated in 0 of 57), completion_date (0), phase (1), lead_sponsor
(3) and a first pass at masking. Publishing a low accuracy on any of them would have looked
like a model finding and been a corpus artefact. The wireframe called its own numbers
illustrative; this file is what the evidence supports.
The set that remains is deliberately MIXED in difficulty. Four fields sit in the record
header and are near-certain; three are buried in prose and are the real test; two are stated
so rarely that the honest answer is almost always 'not found', which is exactly the
behaviour this kit exists to measure.

fields.name: nct_id
fields.hint: The registry identifier, of the form NCT followed by eight digits.

fields.name: condition
fields.hint: The condition or disease under study, as written.

fields.name: primary_outcome
fields.hint: The first primary outcome measure. The measure itself, not its time frame.

fields.name: sex
fields.hint: Which sexes are eligible. ALL when the criteria do not restrict it.

fields.name: minimum_age
fields.hint: The lowest eligible age, as a number of years, e.g. '18 Years'.

fields.name: allocation
fields.hint: Whether participants were assigned to arms at random.

fields.name: enrollment
fields.hint: How many participants were enrolled. Only if the document states a number.

fields.name: masking
fields.hint: The level of blinding. Only if the document states it.
